item.title: Alberta voters decide whether to take a step toward separating from Canada
item.description: In Canada, the oil-rich province of Alberta votes in a referendum that could set it on a path toward separation, as Prime Minister Mark Carney warns of threats to Canadian unity.
item.content:encoded: In Canada, the oil-rich province of Alberta votes in a referendum that could set it on a path toward separation, as Prime Minister Mark Carney warns of threats to Canadian unity.
item.dc:creator: Sheena Rossiter

item.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
item.description: A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.
item.content:encoded:
A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.

(Image credit: Mick Tsikas)

item.title: 2026 midterms could be the most expensive on record. And, Macron condemns protests
item.description: More than $15 billion has been raised in this year's midterm elections. And, France's president is condemning the violent protests erupting across the country.

item.title: Solar power is changing agriculture in Pakistan, but some fear it could cause issues
item.description: Solar power is transforming agriculture in Pakistan. But in a country already facing water scarcity and extreme weather, some fear their widespread use could cause problems.

item.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
item.description: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.

item.title: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.
